title.narrative: India Procurement Capacity Building Program for Karnataka

description.narrative: The purpose of the Grant is to assist the Recipient in supporting procurement capacity development in the State of Karnataka (Karnataka). The activities (the Activities) for which the Grant is given are as follows: Part A: Phase One (estimated to cost US$182,400 equivalent) 1. Conducting procurement capacity needs assessment in Karnataka. 2. Developing a comprehensive training program for addressing the needs identified pursuant to paragraph 1 of this Part A. 3. Starting the learning process by dissemination of the KTPP Act and Rules, the instructions and orders issued on the new initiatives and explain the rationale behind them. 4. Developing and designing training materials (modules), including a procurement manual to serve as a comprehensive guide on the new legislation relating to procurement in Karnataka, and disseminating such training materials. to the Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurements Act 1999 and Rules 2000. 5. Analyzing and identifying state level institutions and trainers in Karnataka for delivering training program and disseminating training materials developed pursuant to paragraphs 2 and 3 respectively of this Part A. 6. Establishing knowledge resource centers at the institutions identified pursuant to paragraph 4 of this Part A and developing a system amongst such institutions for sharing such resources 7. Establish a system for the accreditation of procurement competence based on the completion of the various curricula to the required level pursuant to paragraphs 1 and 2 respectively of this Part A. Part B: Phase Two (estimated to cost US$280,600 equivalent) 1. Building capacity within institutions identified pursuant to paragraph 4 5 of Part A to run training program referred to in paragraph 2 of Part A, through, inter alia, developing and implementing a program to train the trainers; and conducting a series of pilot training programs at such institutions to evaluate trainers, trainees and training materials. 2. Developing and implementing a bench marking system by identification of monitoring indicators and conducting a bench mark survey before the start of training activities to determine the effectiveness of the training program to train the trainers, the pilot training programs. 3. Procuring additional Training equipment. Part C: Phase Three (estimated to cost US$25,000 equivalent) 1. Conducting a review of the existing training program current Training Master Plan of Karnataka, and identifying and implementing necessary changes required in such program in the light of the analysis of the pilot training programs conducted pursuant to paragraph 2 1 of Part B above. 2. Developing a system long term action plan within Karnataka for providing sustained training, with certification, on public procurement. The purpose of the grant is to support the procurement development capacity in the state of Karnataka.
